title: Telemetry runbook and instrumentation closure for intermittent route-level latency cliffs
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Summary: During a capacity regression on 2026-03-12 (inc-2026-0312-console-latency), customer-visible latency cliffs were observed for a subset of console routes. Root cause analysis indicates a combination of (1) missing queue-depth and per-route ingress tagging metrics, (2) sparsely-instrumented RPC spans along the console -> runtime path, and (3) an over-aggregated dashboard that masked hot routes. This ticket captures the action items to close instrumentation gaps, build a targeted runbook for on-call, and add dashboards/alerts to detect the pattern before customer impact.

Context and impact: The incident created ~30 minutes of elevated 95th/99th latency for console routes that handle tenant-specific KV cache priming. Several customers saw increased API error rates and a few support escalations. Impact classified as medium. The immediate mitigation (increase autoscale headroom and temporary rate-limits) reduced customer errors but did not address the blind spots that delayed diagnosis.

Primary goals:
- Add per-route ingress tagging and queue-depth metrics to the console ingress pipeline.
- Expand span coverage and consistent trace correlation keys across console -> runtime -> GPU workers.
- Create a concise runbook describing detection, mitigation, and post-incident checks for route-level latency cliffs.
- Replace the over-aggregated latency dashboard with a tiled view that surfaces top-10 routes by 95th latency and per-route queue/backpressure signals.

Non-goals: deep runtime kernel tuning (handled in separate performance project), user-facing API changes.
acceptance_criteria: Per-route ingress tags (route_id, tenant_id_safe, route_type) are emitted on 100% of console ingress requests and visible in metrics export
Queue depth / backlog metric exposed with 1s resolution and tracked per-route and per-tenant for top 100 routes
Trace coverage increased: console->runtime RPC spans present in >=95% sampled requests for top-traffic routes with correlation id propagation
New dashboard shows top-10 routes by p95 latency, queue depth heatmap, and KV cache eviction rate; actionable alerts created
Runbook written and reviewed by SRE and Console PM, published to Confluence, and added to on-call rotation playbooks
